rv.q: At once hilarious, heartbreaking, and hopeful, Triple Threat feels like one man’s authentic catharsis.
The execution and design of the lighting and sound, especially during the dance/movement parts of the show is superb.
Lane proves to be a remarkable actor and writer.
With those breakthroughs late in Triple Threat, Lane offers one of the most stirring epiphanies seen on stage in a while.
Lane uses his artistic triple threats to share his important story of the triple threats that have threatened his existence and the paths back to recovery.

cn.t: Broadway vet James T. Lane earns strong reviews for this gut-punch solo show about his struggles with addiction, proving himself a triple threat both in traditional theater terms and in confronting being Black, gay, and an addict.
